claim: Neurotensin (Nts) is a neuropeptide acting as a neuromodulator in the brain.
source: Neurotensin (Nts) is a neuropeptide acting as a neuromodulator in the brain.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about neurotensin's role.

claim: Pharmacological studies have identified Nts as a potent hypothermic agent.
source: Pharmacological studies have identified Nts as a potent hypothermic agent.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous pharmacological studies.

claim: The medial preoptic area contains a high density of neurotensinergic neurons and Nts receptors.
source: The medial preoptic area, a region that plays an important role in the control of thermoregulation, contains a high density of neurotensinergic neurons and Nts receptors.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact about the anatomical distribution of neurotensinergic components.

claim: Optogenetic stimulation of preoptic Nts neurons induced a small hyperthermia.
source: In this study, optogenetic stimulation of preoptic Nts neurons induced a small hyperthermia.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study's experiments.

claim: Optogenetic stimulation of preoptic Nts neurons resulted in synaptic release of GABA and net inhibition of the preoptic pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (Adcyap1) neurons firing activity.
source: In vitro, optogenetic stimulation of preoptic Nts neurons resulted in synaptic release of GABA and net inhibition of the preoptic pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (Adcyap1) neurons firing activity.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vitro studies.

claim: GABA-A receptor antagonist or genetic deletion of Slc32a1 (VGAT) in Nts neurons unmasked an excitatory effect that was blocked by a Nts receptor 1 antagonist.
source: GABA-A receptor antagonist or genetic deletion of Slc32a1 (VGAT) in Nts neurons unmasked also an excitatory effect that was blocked by a Nts receptor 1 antagonist.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from pharmacological and genetic manipulation studies.

claim: Stimulation of preoptic Nts neurons lacking Slc32a1 resulted in excitation of Adcyap1 neurons and hypothermia.
source: Stimulation of preoptic Nts neurons lacking Slc32a1 resulted in excitation of Adcyap1 neurons and hypothermia.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from genetic manipulation studies.

claim: Mice lacking Slc32a1 expression in Nts neurons presented changes in the fever response and in the responses to heat or cold exposure as well as an altered circadian rhythm of body temperature.
source: Mice lacking Slc32a1 expression in Nts neurons presented changes in the fever response and in the responses to heat or cold exposure as well as an altered circadian rhythm of body temperature.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from studies in genetically modified mice.

claim: Chemogenetic activation of all Nts neurons in the brain induced a 4–5°C hypothermia, which could be blocked by Nts receptor antagonists in the preoptic area.
source: Chemogenetic activation of all Nts neurons in the brain induced a 4–5°C hypothermia, which could be blocked by Nts receptor antagonists in the preoptic area.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from chemogenetic studies.

claim: Chemogenetic activation of preoptic neurotensinergic projections resulted in robust excitation of preoptic Adcyap1 neurons.
source: Chemogenetic activation of preoptic neurotensinergic projections resulted in robust excitation of preoptic Adcyap1 neurons.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from chemogenetic studies.

claim: Endogenously released Nts can induce potent hypothermia.
source: Taken together, our data demonstrate that endogenously released Nts can induce potent hypothermia and that excitation of preoptic Adcyap1 neurons is the cellular mechanism that triggers this response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Excitation of preoptic Adcyap1 neurons is the cellular mechanism that triggers hypothermia induced by endogenously released Nts.
source: Taken together, our data demonstrate that endogenously released Nts can induce potent hypothermia and that excitation of preoptic Adcyap1 neurons is the cellular mechanism that triggers this response.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: The preoptic area of the hypothalamus plays an important role in CBT regulation by integrating peripheral thermal information and by sending efferent signals that control thermal effector organs.
source: The preoptic area of the hypothalamus plays an important role in CBT regulation by integrating peripheral thermal information and by sending efferent signals that control thermal effector organs (Morrison and Nakamura, 2019; Nakamura et al., 2022a; Tan and Knight, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Via projections to the dorsomedial hypothalamus and rostral raphe pallidus, preoptic neurons control thermogenesis as well as heat loss mechanisms.
source: Via projections to the dorsomedial hypothalamus and rostral raphe pallidus, preoptic neurons control thermogenesis as well as heat loss mechanisms (Morrison, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The preoptic area orchestrates the fever response, an important mechanism for fighting infection or inflammatory disease.
source: The preoptic area also orchestrates the fever response, an important mechanism for fighting infection or inflammatory disease (Morrison and Nakamura, 2019; Saper et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Recent studies have identified populations of preoptic neurons that integrate peripheral thermal information and control the core body temperature (CBT) and play an important role in the fever response to endotoxin.
source: Recent studies have identified populations of preoptic neurons that integrate peripheral thermal information and control the core body temperature (CBT) and play an important role in the fever response to endotoxin (Machado et al., 2020; Moffitt et al., 2018; Nakamura et al., 2022b; Tan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: Neurotensin (Nts) is a 13 aminoacid peptide found in the CNS as well as in the gastrointestinal tract.
source: Neurotensin (Nts) is a 13 aminoacid peptide found in the CNS as well as in the gastrointestinal tract (Vincent et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Nts-producing neurons and their projections are widely distributed in the brain, which may explain the wide variety of effects of this peptide.
source: Nts-producing neurons and their projections are widely distributed in the brain, which may explain the wide variety of effects of this peptide (Schroeder and Leinninger, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and includes speculative reasoning about the implications.

claim: Pharmacological approaches have revealed a role of Nts in analgesia, arousal, blood pressure, feeding, reward, sleep, the stress response and thermoregulation.
source: Pharmacological approaches have revealed a role of Nts in analgesia, arousal, blood pressure, feeding, reward, sleep, the stress response and thermoregulation (Kleczkowska and Lipkowski, 2013; Kyriatzis et al., 2024; Ramirez-Virella and Leinninger, 2021; Torruella-Suárez and McElligott, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous pharmacological studies.

claim: Studies have started to unravel the role played by specific populations of neurotensinergic neurons in feeding and drinking behaviors as well as in sleep and appetitive and reinforcing aspects of motivated behaviors.
source: Recently, studies have started to unravel the role played by specific populations of neurotensinergic neurons in feeding (Chen et al., 2022; Woodworth et al., 2017) and drinking behaviors (Kurt et al., 2022) as well as in sleep (Ma et al., 2019; Zhong et al., 2019) and appetitive and reinforcing aspects of motivated behaviors (McHenry et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to recent studies.

claim: When infused intracerebroventricularly or in the preoptic area Nts induces a 4–5°C hypothermia.
source: When infused intracerebroventricularly or in the preoptic area Nts induces a 4–5°C hypothermia (Gordon et al., 2003; St-Gelais et al., 2006; Tabarean, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The hypothermic effect of Nts was attributed to activation of heat loss mechanisms.
source: The effect was attributed to activation of heat loss mechanisms (Handler et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The medial preoptic area (MPO) expresses high densities of both neurotensinergic neurons and neurotensin receptors.
source: The medial preoptic area (MPO) expresses high densities of both neurotensinergic neurons and neurotensin receptors (Schroeder and Leinninger, 2018; Alexander and Leeman, 1998; Nicot et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A previous study has identified a population of MPO Nts neurons that express Slc32a1 and modulate sexual behavior via projections to the ventral tegmental area.
source: A previous study has identified a population of MPO Nts neurons that express Slc32a1 and modulate sexual behavior via projections to the ventral tegmental area (McHenry et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: MPONts;ChR2 neurons were spontaneously active and the majority of them (16 out of 22 neurons studied) fired mostly doublets or triplets of action potentials.
source: Patch-clamp recordings revealed that MPONts;ChR2 neurons were spontaneously active and the majority of them (16 out of 22 neurons studied) fired mostly doublets or triplets of action potentials (Figure 1A) while the rest fired single action potentials.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from patch-clamp recordings, with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: The average firing rate of MPONts;ChR2 neurons at 36 °C was 4.29±2.45 Hz (n=22).
source: The average firing rate at 36 °C was 4.29±2.45 Hz (n=22).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The average capacitance of MPONts;ChR2 neurons tested was 17.86±2.48 pF (n=22).
source: The average capacitance of the neurons tested was 17.86±2.48 pF (n=22).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: All MPONts;ChR2 neurons tested displayed a low threshold spike (LTS) upon the end of a hyperpolarizing current injection.
source: All neurons tested displayed a low threshold spike (LTS) upon the end of a hyperpolarizing current injection (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from electrophysiological recordings, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Injection of positive currents generated bursts of doublets or triplets of action potentials in MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
source: Injection of positive currents generated bursts of doublets or triplets of action potentials (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from electrophysiological recordings, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Nts transcripts were detected in 7 out of 10 MPONts;ChR2 neurons studied.
source: We could detect Nts transcripts in 7 out of 10 MPONts;ChR2 studied (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from scRT/PCR analysis, with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: Slc32a1 was detected in 8 out of 10 Nts-expressing MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
source: Slc32a1 was detected in 8 out of 10 Nts-expressing neurons (Figure 1C) while none of these cells expressed Slc17a6 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) suggesting that the majority of MPONts;ChR2 are GABAergic.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from scRT/PCR analysis, with reference to Figure 1C.

claim: None of the Nts-expressing MPONts;ChR2 neurons expressed Slc17a6.
source: Slc32a1 was detected in 8 out of 10 Nts-expressing neurons (Figure 1C) while none of these cells expressed Slc17a6 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) suggesting that the majority of MPONts;ChR2 are GABAergic.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from scRT/PCR analysis, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The majority of MPONts;ChR2 are GABAergic.
source: Slc32a1 was detected in 8 out of 10 Nts-expressing neurons (Figure 1C) while none of these cells expressed Slc17a6 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) suggesting that the majority of MPONts;ChR2 are GABAergic.
evidence: This is an inference based on the detection of Slc32a1 and absence of Slc17a6 in the neurons.

claim: Spot illumination of MPONts;ChR2 neurons instantly depolarized them and increased their firing rate in all neurons tested.
source: Spot illumination of MPONts;ChR2 neurons instantly depolarized them and increased their firing rate in all neurons tested (not shown).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from optogenetic stimulation experiments.

claim: Spot illumination of nearby MPONts;ChR2 neurons resulted in a robust decrease in firing rate in 9 out of 30 non-labeled MPO neurons studied or no effect in the others (21 out of 30 neurons studied).
source: Recordings from non-labeled MPO neurons revealed that spot illumination of nearby MPONts;ChR2 neurons resulted in a robust decrease in their firing rate (9 out of 30 neurons studied) or no effect in the others (21 out of 30 neurons studied).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from optogenetic stimulation experiments.

claim: Optogenetic stimulation of nearby MPONts;ChR2 neurons reduced the firing rate of recorded MPO neurons from 5.10±1.32 Hz to 1.39±0.36 Hz (n=9).
source: Overall, optogenetic stimulation of nearby MPONts;ChR2 neurons reduced the firing rate of the recorded MPO neurons from 5.10±1.32 Hz to 1.39±0.36 Hz (n=9).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: In the presence of gabazine, MPO neurons displayed an increase in firing rate in response to photostimulation of MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
source: In the presence of the antagonist, the same neurons displayed the opposite effect, an increase in firing rate in response to photostimulation. Their firing rate was 7.89±2.61 Hz (n=9) in the presence of gabazine and increased to 9.57±2.83 Hz (n=9) during photostimulation (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from pharmacological manipulation experiments, with reference to Figure 2A and B.

claim: The NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 blocked the increase in firing rate induced by photostimulation in the presence of gabazine.
source: Since we have previously found that exogenous Nts applied locally increased the firing activity of MPO neurons by activating NtsR1 (Tabarean, 2020) we have tested the effect of photostimulation in the presence of both gabazine (5 µM) and the NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 (100 nM). The antagonist blocked the effect of photostimulation indicating that the increase in firing rate depended on activation of NtsR1.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from pharmacological manipulation experiments.

claim: The increase in firing rate of MPO neurons in response to photostimulation of MPONts;ChR2 neurons (in the presence of gabazine) depended on activation of NtsR1.
source: The antagonist blocked the effect of photostimulation indicating that the increase in firing rate depended on activation of NtsR1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the blocking effect of the NtsR1 antagonist.

claim: Adcyap1 transcripts were detected in 9 out of 12 MPO neurons excited by photostimulation (in the presence of gabazine) tested.
source: We have detected Adcyap1 transcripts in 9 out of 12 neurons tested. Figure 2C depicts an example of scRT/PCR analysis of a batch of six recorded neurons.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from scRT/PCR analysis, with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Photostimulation of MPONts;ChR2 neurons induced a robust increase in the IPSCs frequency in the presence of glutamate receptor blockers CNQX and AP-5, as well as of the NtsR1 antagonist SR48692.
source: In the presence of the glutamate receptor blockers CNQX (10 µM) and AP-5 (50 µM), as well as of the NtsR1antagonist SR48692 (100 nM), photostimulation MPONts;ChR2 neurons induced a robust increase in the IPSCs frequency (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from voltage-clamp experiments, with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: GABA release from MPONts;ChR2 neurons was not dependent upon excitatory synaptic transmission nor upon activation of NtsR1.
source: These results indicate that GABA release was not dependent neither upon excitatory synaptic transmission nor upon activation of NtsR1, that is it is synaptically released by MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results showing increased IPSCs in the presence of glutamate receptor blockers and NtsR1 antagonist.

claim: GABA is synaptically released by MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
source: These results indicate that GABA release was not dependent neither upon excitatory synaptic transmission nor upon activation of NtsR1, that is it is synaptically released by MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results.

claim: Brief photostimulation (10 s or less) resulted in increased frequency of IPSCs only.
source: We have also found that brief photostimulation (10 s or less) resulted in increased frequency of IPSCs only (Figure 3B and C) while longer photostimulation (30 s or more) additionally activated an inward current (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from voltage-clamp experiments, with reference to Figure 3B and C.

claim: Longer photostimulation (30 s or more) additionally activated an inward current.
source: We have also found that brief photostimulation (10 s or less) resulted in increased frequency of IPSCs only (Figure 3B and C) while longer photostimulation (30 s or more) additionally activated an inward current (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from voltage-clamp experiments, with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: The inward current activated by photostimulation averaged 9.26±2.39 pA (n=10).
source: The inward current was isolated in the presence of extracellular gabazine (5 µM) and averaged 9.26±2.39 pA (n=10).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: The inward current was abolished by bath application of NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 (100 nM).
source: The inward current was abolished by bath application of NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 (100 nM) (Figure 3B and D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from pharmacological manipulation experiments, with reference to Figure 3B and D.

claim: In female MPONts;ChR2 mice, optogenetic stimulation resulted in a robust increase in the frequency of IPSCs followed, with a delay of 20–40 s, by an inward current that averaged 11.3±3.4 pA (n=5).
source: We have carried out a set of experiments in MPONts;ChR2 from female mice and recorded similar results. Optogenetic stimulation resulted in a robust increase in the frequency of IPSCs followed, with a delay of 20–40 s, by an inward current that averaged 11.3±3.4 pA (n=5) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from experiments in female mice, with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: All the optogenetically evoked responses in female MPONts;ChR2 mice were blocked by incubation with gabazine (5 µM) and SR48692 (100 nM).
source: All the optogenetically evoked responses were blocked by incubation with gabazine (5 µM) and SR48692 (100 nM) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from pharmacological manipulation experiments in female mice, with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: None out of 8 MPONts;ChR2 neurons studied presented either IPSCs or an inward current evoked by optogenetic stimulation of other MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
source: Finally, we have recorded from MPONts;ChR2 neurons and stimulated, using spot illumination, a different MPONts;ChR2 neuron to question the presence of reciprocal connections. None out of 8 MPONts;ChR2 neurons studied presented either IPSCs or an inward current evoked by optogenetic stimulation of other MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from optogenetic stimulation experiments.

claim: Thermoregulatory preoptic neurons project to the dorsomedial hypothalamus, arcuate, paraventricular thalamus and to the rostral raphe pallidus to control thermoeffector mechanisms.
source: Thermoregulatory preoptic neurons project to the dorsomedial hypothalamus, arcuate, paraventricular thalamus and to the rostral raphe pallidus to control thermoeffector mechanisms (Nakamura et al., 2022b; Tan et al., 2016; Hrvatin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: No fluorescent signal was detected in the brains of MPONts;eYFP mice in coronal slices at sites where thermoregulatory preoptic neurons project, suggesting that MPONts;eYFP modulate CBT by acting on MPOAdcyap1 neurons.
source: We have examined the brains of MPONts;eYFP mice in coronal slices to identify MPO projections to these sites, however no fluorescent signal was detected suggesting that MPONts;eYFP modulate CBT by acting on MPOAdcyap1 neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of fluorescent signal at projection sites.

claim: Optogenetic activation of Nts neurons in the MPO using MPONts;ChR2 mice resulted in hyperthermia of up to 1.22 ± 0.35 oC when compared with control MPONts;eYFP mice (n=6 mice in each condition).
source: Optogenetic activation of Nts neurons in the MPO using MPONts;ChR2 mice resulted in hyperthermia of up to 1.22 ± 0.35 oC when compared with control MPONts;eYFP mice (n=6 mice in each condition) (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vivo optogenetic experiments, with reference to Figure 4A and B.

claim: Activation of Nts neurons in MPONts;Slc32a1-;ChR2 mice resulted in a decrease in CBT of 1.44 ± 0.29 oC relative to control MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;eYFP mice.
source: To assess the role played by GABA release from MPO Nts neurons in the observed hyperthermia we activated Nts neurons in MPONts;Slc32a1-;ChR2 mice (see Methods). Surprisingly, a decrease in CBT of 1.44 ± 0.29 oC was recorded relative to control MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;eYFP mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vivo optogenetic experiments in genetically modified mice, with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: In female MPONts;ChR2 mice, intra-MPO optogenetic stimulation resulted in a hyperthermia of 1.40 ± 0.62 oC.
source: Similar results were obtained also in female MPONts;ChR2 mice and MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 mice. Intra- MPO optogenetic stimulation resulted in a hyperthermia of 1.40 ± 0.62 oC in MPONts;ChR2 females and in a hypothermia of 1.63 ± 0.22 oC in MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 females (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vivo optogenetic experiments in female mice, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: In female MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 mice, intra-MPO optogenetic stimulation resulted in a hypothermia of 1.63 ± 0.22 oC.
source: Similar results were obtained also in female MPONts;ChR2 mice and MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 mice. Intra- MPO optogenetic stimulation resulted in a hyperthermia of 1.40 ± 0.62 oC in MPONts;ChR2 females and in a hypothermia of 1.63 ± 0.22 oC in MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 females (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vivo optogenetic experiments in female mice, with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The basal electrophysiological properties of MPONts; Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons were similar with those of MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
source: The basal electrophysiological properties of MPONts; Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons were similar with those of MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
evidence: This is a comparison of experimental findings.

claim: MPONts; Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons were spontaneously active, with an average firing rate at 36 °C of 4.79±2.45 Hz (n=26).
source: The neurons were spontaneously active, with an average firing rate at 36 °C of 4.79±2.45 Hz (n=26).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data.

claim: Spot illumination of nearby MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons increased the firing rate of non-labeled MPO neurons (12 out of 26 neurons studied) or had no effect in the others (14 out of 26 neurons).
source: Recordings from non-labeled MPO neurons revealed that spot illumination of nearby MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons increased their firing rate (12 out of 26 neurons studied) or had no effect in the others (14 out of 26 neurons).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from optogenetic stimulation experiments.

claim: Optogenetic stimulation of nearby MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons increased the firing rate of recorded MPO neurons from 5.68±1.66 Hz to 12.20±3.65 Hz (n=12).
source: Overall, optogenetic stimulation of nearby MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons increased the firing rate of the recorded MPO neurons from 5.68±1.66 Hz to 12.20±3.65 Hz (n=12) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data, with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: The increase in firing rate induced by optogenetic stimulation of MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons was blocked by preincubation with the NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 (100 nM).
source: This effect was blocked by preincubation with the NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 (100 nM; Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from pharmacological manipulation experiments, with reference to Figure 5A and B.

claim: Photostimulation of MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons activated an inward current which was abolished by bath application of NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 (100 nM).
source: In voltage-clamp experiments photostimulation activated an inward current which was abolished by bath application of NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 (100 nM) (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from voltage-clamp experiments, with reference to Figure 5C and D.

claim: Adcyap1 transcripts were detected in 8 out of 11 neurons excited by photostimulation of MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons tested.
source: Using s.c. RT/PCR assays we have detected Adcyap1 transcripts in 8 out of 11 neurons excited by photostimulation tested.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from scRT/PCR analysis.

claim: Nts and Slc32a1 transcripts overlapped in control Ntscre Slc32a1+/+ tissue while there was no colocalization in tissue from Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice.
source: We have studied the presence of Slc32a1 and Nts transcripts in MPO slices from Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice and in control Ntscre Slc32a1+/+ mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1). Nts and Slc32a1 transcripts overlapped in control tissue while there was no colocalization in tissue from Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from RNAscope analysis, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The LPS-induced fever was significantly different in NtsSlc32a1-/- mice when compared with that of wild-type littermates Ntscre Slc32a1+/+.
source: The LPS-induced fever was significantly different in NtsSlc32a1-/- mice when compared with that of wild-type littermates Ntscre Slc32a1+/+ (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vivo fever response experiments, with reference to Figure 6A.

claim: During the intermediate and late phases of fever, the CBT was significantly lower in Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice.
source: During the intermediate and late phases of fever, the CBT was significantly lower in Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vivo fever response experiments, with reference to Figure 6A.

claim: During heat exposure the CBT increased at a faster rate in Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice than in Ntscre Slc32a1+/+ mice.
source: During heat exposure the CBT increased at a faster rate in Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice than in Ntscre Slc32a1+/+ mice (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vivo heat exposure experiments, with reference to Figure 6B.

claim: The Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice and Ntscre Slc32a1+/+ mice reached 41.5 oC within 1.33±0.04 hr and 1.53±0.04 hr, respectively (Kruskal-Wallis, p=2.14 × 10–4, n=9 mice in each group).
source: The Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice and Ntscre Slc32a1+/+ mice reached 41.5 oC within 1.33±0.04 hr and 1.53±0.04 hr, respectively (Kruskal-Wallis, p=2.14 × 10–4, n=9 mice in each group).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: The Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice displayed significantly higher CBT (by ~0.5 oC) after 45 min of heat exposure.
source: The Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice displayed significantly higher CBT (by ~0.5 oC) after 45 min of heat exposure (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vivo heat exposure experiments, with reference to Figure 6B.

claim: The circadian CBT profile of Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice was altered relative to that of Ntscre Slc32a1+/+ mice: the active phase started ~1 hr earlier and ended ~3 hr later.
source: The circadian CBT profile of Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice was also altered relative to that of Ntscre Slc32a1+/+ mice: the active phase started ~1 hr earlier and ended ~3 hr later (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from circadian rhythm monitoring, with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: During a 3 hr exposure in a cold room at 4°C the control mice displayed a gradual decrease in CBT which stabilized at 33-34 oC by third hour of the cold exposure.
source: During a 3 hr exposure in a cold room at 4°C the two mouse lines displayed strikingly different CBT responses (Figure 6D). The control mice displayed a gradual decrease in CBT which stabilized at 33-34 oC by third hour of the cold exposure.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vivo cold exposure experiments, with reference to Figure 6D.

claim: Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice displayed a hyperthermia of 37.4°C at the beginning of the cold exposure experiment followed by a slow decline that reached ~35 oC at the end of the three hours.
source: In contrast, Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice displayed a hyperthermia of 37.4°C at the beginning of the experiment followed by a slow decline that reached ~35 oC at the end of the three hours.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vivo cold exposure experiments.

claim: Upon return to vivarium after cold exposure the CBT of control mice returned to 37 °C while the Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice displayed a transient hyperthermia to 39°C.
source: Upon return to vivarium the CBT of controls returned to 37 °C while the Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice displayed a transient hyperthermia to 39°C.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from in vivo cold exposure experiments.

claim: Activation of central Ntscre hM3Dlox/lox neurons induced a potent hypothermia of 4.8 ± 0.6 °C relative to Nts-cre mice (control).
source: Activation of central Ntscre hM3Dlox/lox neurons induced a potent hypothermia of 4.8 ± 0.6 °C relative to Nts-cre mice (control) (Figure 7A), value comparable with that obtained with MPO infusions of exogenous Nts (Tabarean, 2020).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from chemogenetic activation experiments, with reference to Figure 7A.

claim: The NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 (300 nM, 100 nl) decreased the chemogenetically induced hypothermia by 41% relative to control.
source: The NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 (300 nM, 100 nl, blue trace) decreased the chemogenetically induced hypothermia by 41% relative to control (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from pharmacological manipulation experiments, with reference to Figure 7B.

claim: Following intra-MPO injections of NTSR2 antagonist NTRC 824 (200 nM, 100 nl) the CNO-induced hypothermia was decreased by 32% relative to control.
source: Following intra-MPO injections of NTSR2 antagonist NTRC 824 (200 nM, 100 nl, black trace) the CNO-induced hypothermia was decreased by 32% relative to control (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from pharmacological manipulation experiments, with reference to Figure 7B.

claim: When the two doses of antagonists (NtsR1 and NtsR2) were infused together the chemogenetically-induced hypothermia decreased by 76%.
source: When the two doses of antagonists were infused together the chemogenetically-induced hypothermia decreased by 76% (Figure 7B, red trace).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from pharmacological manipulation experiments, with reference to Figure 7B.

claim: The MPO accounts for most of the hypothermia induced by Ntscre hM3Dlox/lox neurons and both receptor subtypes (NtsR1 and NtsR2) play an important role.
source: These results indicate that the MPO accounts for most of the hypothermia induced by Ntscre hM3Dlox/lox neurons and that both receptor subtypes play an important role.
evidence: This is an inference based on the blocking effects of NtsR1 and NtsR2 antagonists in the MPO.

claim: Bath application of CNO excited 9 out 20 MPO non-labeled neurons studied in slices from NtscrehM3Dlox/lox mice and had no effect in the others.
source: To understand the mechanisms by which chemogenetic activation of NtscrehM3Dlox/lox neurons induced hypothermia, we have studied the effect of CNO on the activity of MPO non-labeled neurons in acute slices from NtscrehM3Dlox/lox mice. Bath application of CNO excited 9 out 20 neurons studied and had no effect in the others.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from chemogenetic activation experiments in slices.

claim: The average firing rate of MPO neurons increased from 4.15±2.95 Hz to 10.63±5.83 Hz (n=9, ANOVA, F(1/16)=8.99 p=8.52 × 10–3) in response to CNO (3 µM).
source: The average firing rate increased from 4.15±2.95 Hz to 10.63±5.83 Hz (n=9, ANOVA, F(1/16)=8.99 p=8.52 × 10–3) in response to CNO (3 µM) (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data with statistical analysis, with reference to Figure 7D.

claim: Adcyap1 transcripts were identified in seven of the nine neurons excited by CNO tested.
source: S.c. RT/PCR assays identified Adcyap1 transcripts in seven of the nine neurons excited by CNO tested.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from scRT/PCR analysis.

claim: Bath application of CNO (3 µM) activated an inward current and potently increased the frequencies and amplitudes of both sEPSCs and sIPSCs.
source: In voltage-clamp experiments bath application of CNO (3 µM) activated an inward current and potently increased the frequencies and amplitudes of both sEPSCs and sIPSCs (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from voltage-clamp experiments, with reference to Figure 7E.

claim: The frequencies of sEPSCs and sIPSCs increased from 2.76±1.16 Hz to 9.14±5.36 Hz and 1.98±1.43 Hz to 8.84±6.38 Hz, respectively (n=6).
source: The frequencies of sEPSCs and sIPSCs increased from 2.76±1.16 Hz to 9.14±5.36 Hz and 1.98±1.43 Hz to 8.84±6.38 Hz, respectively (n=6) (Figure 7F and H).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data, with reference to Figure 7F and H.

claim: The amplitudes of sIPSCs and sEPSCs increased from 13.61±4.51 pA to 29.60±5.32 pA and 13.02±3.99 pA to 22.12±5.53 pA, respectively (n=6).
source: The amplitudes of sIPSCs and sEPSCs increased from 13.61±4.51 pA to 29.60±5.32 pA and 13.02±3.99 pA to 22.12±5.53 pA, respectively (n=6)(Figure 7G,I).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from experimental data, with reference to Figure 7G,I.

claim: The NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 (100 nM) abolished the inward current activated by CNO and significantly reduced the effect on the frequency of sIPSCs.
source: The NtsR1 antagonist SR48692 (100 nM) abolished the inward current activated by CNO (Figure 7E, middle trace) and significantly reduced the effect on the frequency of sIPSCs (Figure 7H).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from pharmacological manipulation experiments, with reference to Figure 7E and 7H.

claim: The NtsR2 antagonist NTRC 824 (100 nM) did not change the inward current activated by CNO but significantly decreased the amplitude of sEPSCs.
source: The NtsR2 antagonist NTRC 824 (100 nM) did not change the inward current activated by CNO but significantly decreased the amplitude of sEPSCs (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from pharmacological manipulation experiments, with reference to Figure 7G.

claim: MPO Nts neurons are GABAergic as indicated by detection of Slc32a1 transcripts as well as by the activation of gabazine-sensitive IPSCs in postsynaptic neurons in response to spot illumination of MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
source: In this study we have characterized a novel population of MPO neurons that express Nts (MPONts). These neurons are GABAergic as indicated by detection of Slc32a1 transcripts as well as by the activation of gabazine-sensitive IPSCs in postsynaptic neurons in response to spot illumination of MPONts;ChR2 neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple experimental findings.

claim: MPO Nts neurons have a tendency to burst in response to depolarization, a characteristic of neurosecretory neurons.
source: Interestingly, this population had a tendency to burst in response to depolarization, a characteristic of neurosecretory neurons (Armstrong et al., 2010; Black et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data with supporting citations.

claim: In response to optogenetic stimulation MPONts;ChR2 neurons released both GABA and Nts as indicated by pharmacological experiments.
source: In response to optogenetic stimulation MPONts;ChR2 neurons released both GABA and Nts as indicated by pharmacological experiments.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on pharmacological experimental findings.

claim: Increased frequency of IPSCs was detected instantaneously upon photostimulation while an inward current was activated after 20–40 s, indicating a differential timecourse of action.
source: Postsynaptically, increased frequency of IPSCs was detected instantaneously upon photostimulation while an inward current was activated after 20–40 s, indicating a differential timecourse of action.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with an inference about the differential timecourse.

claim: Nts may act to limit and/or shorten the inhibitory effect of GABA on the activity of the postsynaptic neurons following increased burst of activity of MPONts neurons.
source: In view of its slower timecourse of action, Nts may act to limit and/or shorten the inhibitory effect of GABA on the activity of the postsynaptic neurons following increased burst of activity of MPONts neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The net effect during photostimulation was a decrease in the firing rate of the postsynaptic neuron, an increase in firing rate being unmasked only upon ending photostimulation or in the presence of gabazine.
source: Nevertheless, the net effect during photostimulation was a decrease in the firing rate of the postsynaptic neuron, an increase in firing rate being unmasked only upon ending photostimulation or in the presence of gabazine.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental findings.

claim: The inhibition-excitation sequence observed is compatible with a scenario where the postsynaptic neuron is inhibited if the presynaptic neurotensinergic neurons are active and quickly activated upon the end of this presynaptic spiking.
source: The inhibition-excitation sequence observed here is compatible with a scenario where the postsynaptic neuron is inhibited if the presynaptic neurotensinergic neurons are active and quickly activated upon the end of this presynaptic spiking.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: A temporal sequence where fast inhibition precedes a slower excitation allows to quickly reset the membrane potential of the postsynaptic neurons making them ready to respond to new stimuli.
source: In more general terms, a temporal sequence where fast inhibition precedes a slower excitation allows to quickly reset the membrane potential of the postsynaptic neurons making them ready to respond to new stimuli.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on general principles of neurophysiology.

claim: The initial inhibition can reset or synchronize neural activity, allowing the subsequent excitation to produce more precisely timed spiking assuming the process occurs simultaneously across a population of neurons.
source: The initial inhibition can also reset or synchronize neural activity, allowing the subsequent excitation to produce more precisely timed spiking assuming the process occurs simultaneously across a population of neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on general principles of neurophysiology.

claim: The sequence of inhibition followed by excitation can contribute to generating and maintaining rhythmic activity in neural networks and create oscillatory patterns at specific frequencies, depending on those of the synaptic input.
source: Alternatively, the sequence of inhibition followed by excitation can contribute to generating and maintaining rhythmic activity in neural networks and create oscillatory patterns at specific frequencies, depending on those of the synaptic input.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on general principles of neurophysiology.

claim: The overall responsiveness of a neural circuit can be influenced by rapid inhibition to reduce gain followed by excitation to increase it.
source: Finally, the overall responsiveness of a neural circuit can be influenced by rapid inhibition to reduce gain followed by excitation to increase it.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on general principles of neurophysiology.

claim: MPONts neurons did not present reciprocal connections instead, they appeared to synapse onto MPOAdcyap1 neurons.
source: In terms of local neuronal networks, MPONts neurons did not present reciprocal connections instead, they appeared to synapse onto MPOAdcyap1 neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental findings.

claim: Adcyap1 has been identified as a marker of preoptic thermoregulatory neurons activated in a warm environment and also during torpor.
source: Adcyap1 has been identified as a marker of preoptic thermoregulatory neurons activated in a warm environment (Tan et al., 2016) and also during torpor (Hrvatin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Activation of MPOAdcyap1 neurons induces hypothermia.
source: Activation of MPOAdcyap1 neurons induces hypothermia (Tan et al., 2016; Hrvatin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Adcyap1 is expressed in several subpopulations of neurons, representing a large proportion of the entire preoptic population.
source: However, Adcyap1 is expressed in several subpopulations of neurons, representing a large proportion of the entire preoptic population (Moffitt et al., 2018; Hrvatin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Recent studies have identified a subpopulation of the MPOAdcyap1 neurons that expresses the EP3 prostanoid receptors, is activated in warm environment and inhibited in a cold environment.
source: Recent studies have identified a subpopulation of the MPOAdcyap1 neurons that expresses the EP3 prostanoid receptors, is activated in warm environment and inhibited in a cold environment (Nakamura et al., 2022b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: The subpopulation of MPOAdcyap1 neurons expressing EP3 receptors plays a critical role in the initiation of the fever response.
source: This population plays a critical role in the initiation of the fever response (Machado et al., 2020; Nakamura et al., 2022b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Modulating the activity of preoptic EP3 neurons up or down induces hypothermia or hyperthermia, respectively.
source: Modulating the activity of preoptic EP3 neurons up or down induces hypothermia or hyperthermia, respectively (Nakamura et al., 2022b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: It is possible that MPONts neurons overlap with a previously hypothesized population of inhibitory neurons that receive peripheral cold input and project to EP3 neurons to trigger thermogenesis and inhibit heat loss.
source: It is possible that MPONts neurons overlap with a previously hypothesized population of inhibitory neurons that receive peripheral cold input and project to EP3 neurons to trigger thermogenesis and inhibit heat loss (Morrison and Nakamura, 2019; Nakamura et al., 2022a).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with supporting citations.

claim: Photostimulation of MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons, which caused a net excitation of MPOAdcyap1 neurons, resulted in hypothermia, supporting the idea that their excitation induces hypothermia.
source: In contrast, photostimulation of MPONts;Slc32a1-/-;ChR2 neurons, which caused a net excitation of MPOAdcyap1 neurons, resulted in hypothermia, supporting the idea that their excitation induces hypothermia (Tan et al., 2016; Hrvatin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental findings with supporting citations.

claim: In the preoptic area, GABA exerts complex effects on CBT depending on the environmental context and the specific neuronal subpopulation involved.
source: Numerous studies have revealed that, in the preoptic area, GABA exerts complex effects on CBT depending on the environmental context and the specific neuronal subpopulation involved (Frosini et al., 2004; Ishiwata et al., 2005; Osaka, 2004; Zhao et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: GABA signaling from neurotensinergic neurons is involved in the hyperthermic mechanisms activated during fever.
source: The fever response to endotoxin, when compared with the control, was characterized by lower CBT during the intermediate and late phases of the fever suggesting that GABA signaling is involved in the hyperthermic mechanisms activated. This finding is in line with the previous reports that preoptic GABA can induce thermogenesis (Ishiwata et al., 2005; Osaka, 2004); however, it is in disagreement with observations that the induction of fever is associated with decreased synaptic inhibition in the preoptic area (Osaka, 2008; Tabarean et al., 2004).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental findings with supporting and contrasting citations.

claim: Preoptic GABA can induce thermogenesis.
source: This finding is in line with the previous reports that preoptic GABA can induce thermogenesis (Ishiwata et al., 2005; Osaka, 2004); however, it is in disagreement with observations that the induction of fever is associated with decreased synaptic inhibition in the preoptic area (Osaka, 2008; Tabarean et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The induction of fever is associated with decreased synaptic inhibition in the preoptic area.
source: This finding is in line with the previous reports that preoptic GABA can induce thermogenesis (Ishiwata et al., 2005; Osaka, 2004); however, it is in disagreement with observations that the induction of fever is associated with decreased synaptic inhibition in the preoptic area (Osaka, 2008; Tabarean et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: It is possible that both mechanisms (GABA-induced thermogenesis and decreased synaptic inhibition) influence CBT during fever with the former playing a prevalent role in the intermediate and later phases.
source: It is possible that both mechanisms influence CBT during fever with the former playing a prevalent role in the intermediate and later phases.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation to reconcile conflicting findings.

claim: In a warm environment preoptic release of GABA decreases and exogenous GABA-A antagonists applied locally have hyperthermic effects.
source: In a warm environment preoptic release of GABA decreases and exogenous GABA-A antagonists applied locally have hyperthermic effects (Ishiwata et al., 2005), thus Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox would be expected to have a higher CBT during a heat challenge.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: In a warm environment GABA release from neurotensinergic neurons is involved in the control of heat loss mechanisms.
source: Indeed, we observed that during heat exposure the CBT of Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice increased significantly faster than in the controls suggesting that in a warm environment GABA release from neurotensinergic neurons is involved in the control of heat loss mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental findings.

claim: Previous studies have revealed increased endogenous release of GABA in the preoptic area during cold exposure and hypothermic effects of exogenous GABA-A antagonist in a cold environment.
source: Previous studies have revealed increased endogenous release of GABA in the preoptic area during cold exposure and hypothermic effects of exogenous GABA-A antagonist in a cold environment (Ishiwata et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: While an increase in preoptic GABA concentration induces hyperthermia, at all ambient temperatures, a widespread central increase in GABA is hypothermic.
source: However, while an increase in preoptic GABA concentration induces hyperthermia, at all ambient temperatures, a widespread central increase in GABA is hypothermic (Frosini et al., 2004; Nikolov and Yakimova, 2011), therefore it is possible that Slc32a1 deletion in Nts neurons outside of the MPO may impact CBT during cold exposure and/or that the respective regions are differentially recruited during distinct thermoregulatory mechanisms.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: It is possible that Slc32a1 deletion in Nts neurons outside of the MPO may impact CBT during cold exposure and/or that the respective regions are differentially recruited during distinct thermoregulatory mechanisms.
source: However, while an increase in preoptic GABA concentration induces hyperthermia, at all ambient temperatures, a widespread central increase in GABA is hypothermic (Frosini et al., 2004; Nikolov and Yakimova, 2011), therefore it is possible that Slc32a1 deletion in Nts neurons outside of the MPO may impact CBT during cold exposure and/or that the respective regions are differentially recruited during distinct thermoregulatory mechanisms.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation to explain unexpected findings.

claim: Neurotensinergic neurons, possibly in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, play a role in the control of circadian rhythm.
source: Finally, Ntscre Slc32a1lox/lox mice have entered the 'up' phase of the circadian CBT rhythm earlier and ended it later when compared to the control, supporting a role of neurotensinergic neurons, possibly in the suprachiasmatic nucleus, in the control of circadian rhythm (Meyer-Spasche et al., 2002; Yamada et al., 1995).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental findings with supporting citations.

claim: Stimulation of neurotensinergic neurons in the MPO is not sufficient to induce hypothermia although this region represents the locus where the hypothermia is triggered.
source: Taken together our results suggest that stimulation of neurotensinergic neurons in the MPO is not sufficient to induce hypothermia although this region represents the locus where the hypothermia is triggered.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The amplitude and duration of the hypothermia observed when activating all central Ntscre hM3Dlox/lox neurons is reminiscent of the characteristics of the torpor state.
source: The amplitude and duration of the hypothermia oberved when activating all central Ntscre hM3Dlox/lox neurons is reminiscent of the characteristics of the torpor state.
evidence: This is an observation comparing experimental findings to a known physiological state.

claim: A previous study has identified a population of preoptic Adcyap1 neurons is involved in the entry in the torpor state.
source: A previous study has identified a population of preoptic Adcyap1 neurons is involved in the entry in the torpor state (Hrvatin et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: It is possible that neurotensinergic projections to preoptic Adcyap1 neurons are involved in the initiation of torpor state.
source: Since in this study we found that preoptic Adcyap1 neurons receive excitatory input from neurotensinegic neurons outside the preoptic area, it is possible that these projections are involved in the initiation of torpor state.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on experimental findings.

claim: CNO increased the frequency and amplitudes of sEPSCs in addition to the actions observed during photostimulation of MPONts;ChR2.
source: Experiments at the cellular level showed that locally applied CNO in slices from Ntscre hM3Dlox/lox mice had a net excitatory effect in nearby MPOAdcyap1 neurons. In addition to the actions observed during photostimulation of MPONts;ChR2, namely increased sIPSCs frequency and an inward current, CNO also increased the frequency and amplitudes of sEPSCs recorded in MPOAdcyap1 neurons.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from chemogenetic activation experiments.

claim: The increase in sEPSCs may be due to activation of glutamatergic projections from brain regions that contain glutamatergic Ntscre hM3Dlox/lox neurons.
source: This may be due to activation of glutamatergic projections from brain regions that contain glutamatergic Ntscre hM3Dlox/lox neurons. Such neurons have been identified in the posterior thalamus and in the ventrolateral periaqueductal gray (Ma et al., 2019; Zhong et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with supporting citations.

claim: Some of the parabrachial nucleus neurons' glutamatergic projections are also neurotensinergic.
source: It is also possible that some of the parabrachial nucleus neurons' glutamatergic projections (Yang et al., 2020) are also neurotensinegic.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with a supporting citation.

claim: It is likely that the chemogenetic stimulation of MPO Ntscre hM3Dlox/lox neurons and projections elevates the local Nts concentration to a level that activates the low affinity NtsR2.
source: It is likely that the chemogenetic stimulation of MPO Ntscre hM3Dlox/lox neurons and projections elevates the local Nts concentration to a level that activates the low affinity NtsR2.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on experimental findings.

claim: NtsR2 receptors are expressed in MPO astrocytes and upon activation stimulate glutamate release from nearby synaptic terminals as observed when exogenous Nts is applied locally.
source: These receptors are expressed in MPO astrocytes and upon activation stimulate glutamate release from nearby synaptic terminals as observed when exogenous Nts is applied locally (Tabarean, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.
